How it works

From a sentence to a model you can keep editing.

Claude works through PolyForm rather than around it. The same model continues in the browser when you are ready to take over.

01

Connect PolyForm to Claude

Add PolyForm as a custom connector in Claude and sign in with your Google account.

02

Ask in plain words

Describe the building, the garden or the change you want. Claude builds it in your account.

03

Check, then open it

Claude shows a 3D view and a floor plan of every level. Open the model in PolyForm to keep going.

04

Keep going with any change

Everything PolyForm can do, Claude can ask for: restyle a door or window, reshape the terrain, turn on procedural grass or a wildflower meadow, or change the weather.

What a prompt actually does

It uses the same tools you do.

Requests are translated into PolyForm actions. That makes the result inspectable, editable and compatible with the rest of the modelling workflow.

Create01

“Build me an L-shaped house, two storeys, with four bedrooms and a bathroom upstairs.”

create_model add_room add_opening add_stairs add_roof
Change02

“Add a bathroom off the upstairs landing, three metres by two.”

add_room add_opening
Visualise03

“Turn on a wildflower meadow at the back, and set it to a rainy afternoon.”

set_appearance set_weather
Claude result
The same editable PolyForm model continues through every prompt

Final imagery can show the initial model and a second prompt changing that same project, making the continuing-model workflow immediately visible.

What Claude can do

Built on PolyForm’s own toolset.

The connector can inspect the model, build with native tools, change appearance and weather, and preview the result before you open it.

The last 20 versions of a model are retained, so a change can be stepped back when needed.

The complete sdk object

Every method in the Developer Console’s sdk object, grouped by subsystem, with its full signature and return type — 192 methods across 15 groups.

GROUPS

sdk

Primitives, materials, lighting, notes and view control. Available directly on `sdk`, with no namespace prefix.

sdk.architecture

Walls, rooms, doors, windows, stairs, roofs and timber framing.

sdk.landscape

Terrain, planting, site furniture, fences, ponds and patios.

sdk.materials

PBR materials and edge-line rendering.

sdk.measurement

Dimensions, distance and units.

sdk.toolbars

Build your own toolbars with your own icons (the Developer Extensibility Suite's Custom toolbars).

sdk.selection

Selecting, grouping and transforming objects.

sdk.camera

Camera projection, views and depth clipping.

sdk.ai

AI Generate, AI Renderer and the assistant panel.

sdk.scene

Scene export/import, history and stats.

sdk.outliner

Introspect the grouping and hierarchy the Outliner panel shows.

sdk.blockKit

PolyForm's built-in LEGO-style stud-block catalog and placement tool.

sdk.text

Flat text labels and solid 3D letters, as the Text and 3D Text tools place them.

sdk.drawing

Drawn geometry: lines, arcs and surfaces, and push/pull on their faces. Points are [x, y, z] in metres. Faces are numbered, and the same steps on the same drawing give the same numbers.

sdk.worldView

Real places: a 3D site (real ground and existing buildings, up to 200 m square), or the flat Google Maps overlay under the model.
